newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila city ferry operator to get govt concessions.
newsitem.headline: Manila city ferry operator to get govt concessions.

text.p: The Board of Investments (BOI) said on Wednesday Asia Amalgamated Holdings Corp's inter-island shipping project would get fiscal incentives such as a minimum three percent duty on imported capital equipment.
The project, costing 969.5 million pesos, is being undertaken by its wholly-owned unit, Marilag Transport Systems Inc.

Marilag will operate ferries within Pasig river, Laguna de Bay and Manila Bay. It will serve as an alternative to land travel in the busy streets of Manila due to the worsening traffic situation, the BOI said.

The project, which will start commercial operations in 1997, will involve 14 air-conditioned ferries and the construction of various terminals under a build-lease-transfer contract with the government.
Asia Amalgamated is the financial services company of the Gow family, majority owner of Uniwide Holdings Inc.
